author: 阿星
content:
## 冷启动：6年 indie hacker 的孤独路

Thomas 做 indie hacker 六年了。

Since early 2024，doing it almost full-time。

Launched dozens of projects。

Most failed，and totally fine with that！

Always been passionate about creating things。

During studies in 2019，started building Uneed as simple directory of frontend development tools。

At first，just way to learn and experiment with NuxtJS。

Framework wasn't familiar with at time。

Would add one new tool each day and developers could discover fresh resources。

As site grew，started receiving tool submissions through Google Form。

Volume quickly became overwhelming。

Led to implement waiting list。

Decided to offer paid "skip the line" option。

This was pivotal moment。

He remembers perfectly：

Realized had passion for building products。

And could make living with it。

Realization shaped entire career trajectory。

While still needed steady income after graduation。

Made conscious decision to work as freelance developer rather than full-time job。

Gave flexibility to continue building and experimenting with own products。

Set foundation for journey as indie hacker。

## 反直觉：从目录到站，收入先腰斩

Now，Uneed takes up most of his time。

Product launch platform built and iterated on for past five years。

Think of it as alternative to Product Hunt。

Where makers showcase products and users discover new ones every day。

Initial version intentionally simple。

Both in concept and execution。

Designed this way because wanted to validate idea with minimal technical investment。

Site was essentially curated list of tools with basic submission functionality。

Nothing fancy，but served purpose perfectly！

First four years，strategy was automate as much as possible。

Spending minimal time on maintenance。

Probably spent only about 2 hours per week on project。

Allowed keep project running smoothly while focusing on other projects and freelance work。

Which was primary source of income at time。

Everything changed January 2024。

Uneed started gaining significant traction。

Coincided with end of freelance contract。

Presented crucial question：

Time to go all-in on indie hacking？

Noticed two important things：

1. Product Hunt losing momentum and facing increasing criticism from indie hacker community
2. Uneed's SEO starting to perform really well

Project generating around $2,000 monthly with minimal effort at time。

Operating costs less than $50 per month。

Excellent margins。

So decided to go all in。

Transformed from simple directory into full product launch platform。

Transformation represented significant technical challenge。

Required much more sophisticated development work than original version。

Big step up in complexity。

But timing and market conditions made it feel like right move。

## 暴击：收入从$1917跌到$870，但他挺住了

When decided to pivot from directory to launch platform。

Revenue dropped dramatically。

Fell from $1,917 in January to $870 in March。

Tempted to revert back to old model multiple times。

But something kept telling him：

"This HAS to work。"

Kept pushing and persistence finally paid off in September。

Both traffic and revenue reached new records。

In October，revenue was $6,738。

Looking back at journey，biggest regret is waiting four years before making pivot。

Why wait so long？

As indie hackers，greatest strength is ability to move quickly and adapt。

When spot opportunity，should seize immediately。

Even if means completely changing product。

If had made transition earlier，Uneed would likely be much further ahead today。

Experience taught valuable lesson：

While slow and steady growth good。

Shouldn't let it prevent from making bold moves when market shows clear signals。

##  punchline：别 quit 工作，别学太多代码

Two things instrumental to success this year。

First one might make laugh because surprisingly simple。

But genuinely believes wouldn't be where is today without it。

Organizes work using Kanban board in Todoist。

Three columns：bucket、todo、doing。

First two columns typically filled with numerous tickets try to regularly sort and prioritize。

However，prioritizing tasks when working solo incredibly challenging。

He'd argue it's one of most difficult aspects of being indie hacker。

Around May or June，made drastic decision：

Only prioritize features directly contributing to growth。

Went through entire board and tagged all tickets with "growth" if potential to increase Uneed's traffic。

Meant putting aside some exciting new features and non-urgent bugs。

To give example，responding to this interview within 24 hours of receiving request。

Because immediately prioritized as "growth" task。

**Don't do these things：**

Don't quit job！

See too many people burning through savings trying to build next big thing。

Keep steady income stream，whether full-time job or freelancing gigs。

Amazed how much clearer can think about product when not constantly stressing about paying next month's rent。

Here's counter-intuitive advice wish someone had given earlier：

Don't spend too much time learning to code。

Yes，technical skills important。

But learning to sell is WAY more crucial。

See brilliant developers building amazing products nobody uses。

Because never learned how to market them。

Can always improve code later。

But without users，don't have business。

Spend as much time learning marketing and sales as learning technical skills。
